question: Walking at (3)/(5) of his normal speed from his home, Vishal is 24 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 3/5 ⇒ Time ratio = 5/3

Extra time = (5/3 − 1) = 2/3 of usual time

⇒ (2/3) of usual time = 24 min

⇒ Usual time = 24 × (3/2) = 36 min

**∴ Answer = 36 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = (3/5) of normal speed; Extra time = 24 min

**Formula used:**

Time ∝ 1/Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let usual time = t

⇒ New time = t × (5/3)

⇒ Extra time = t × (5/3 − 1)

⇒ t × (2/3) = 24

⇒ t = 24 × (3/2)

⇒ t = 36 min

**∴ The correct answer is 36 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

Time ∝ 1/Speed for fixed distance

Ratio Trick

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a

Extra Time

Extra time = New time − Original time

Quick Method

Use fractional difference directly to find original time
